The '''Euler Lecture''' (''Euler-Vorlesung in Sanssouci'') is a mathematics lecture given at an annual event at the [[University of Potsdam]] (''Universität Potsdam''). The event, initiated in 1993,<ref name=EulerLecture>{{cite web|url=http://www.euler-lecture.berlin |title=Euler-Vorlesung: Startseite}}</ref> is organized by the ''Universität Potsdam, Institut for Mathematik'', the ''[[Humboldt University of Berlin|Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin]], Institut für Mathematik'', and the ''{{ill|Berliner Mathematische Gesellschaft|de}}'' with the assistance of several other organizations, including the ''[[Freie Universität Berlin]], Fachbereich Mathematik und Informatik'', the ''[[Technische Universität Berlin]]'', Institut für Mathematic, the [[Zuse Institute Berlin|''Zuse-Institut Berlin'']] (ZIB), and the ''[[Deutsche Mathematiker-Vereinigung]]'' (DMV).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euler-lecture.berlin/veranstalter.html |title=Euler-Vorlesung: Veranstalter }}</ref> The mathematical lecturer is selected by a distinguished  jury. The event also contains a historical lecture (''Vortrag'') and a musical program supporting the event.<ref name=EulerLecture/>

The Euler Lecture is named in honor of [[Leonhard Euler]], who spent the years from 1741 to 1766 in Berlin and during that time wrote approximately 380 works.<ref name=MacTutor>{{MacTutor|id=Euler|title=Leonhard Euler}}</ref> Among other things, Euler worked for many years as director of the mathematics section at the [[Prussian Academy of Sciences]] and as a consultant at the court of [[Frederick the Great]] in [[Potsdam]].<ref name=EulerLecture/><ref name=MacTutor/>

The Euler Lecture should not be confused with the Ulf von Euler Lecture, an annual lecture sponsored by the [[Karolinska Institute]] and named in honor of the Swedish physiologist [[Ulf von Euler]] (1905–1983).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ki.se/en/fyfa/the-ulf-von-euler-lecture |title=The Ulf von Euler lecture &#124; Karolinska Institutet }}</ref>
